analysis.title: Cross-Asset Dispatches: Global Fixed Income Supply Tracker
key_insights: AI-related corporate credit supply remains elevated, but MS sees investment grade (IG) as safer than high yield (HY) as higher rates pressure weaker-quality borrowers. The credit strategy team now prefers IG over HY.
IG supply remains concentrated in Tech and Communications. More "programmatic" hyperscaler issuance should make absorption of new issuance more manageable.
Government bond supply and yields continue to diverge across markets. Inflation, monetary policy, and term premia remain more important drivers of yields than supply.
Over the past three months, credit spread moves have been largely disconnected from net issuance (Exhibit 1).
Higher relative government bond net issuance has not been associated with higher yields over the past 12 months or the past 1 month (Exhibits 2 and 3).

The report tracks net issuance, cumulative year-to-date issuance, amount outstanding, and yield or spread moves versus issuance for USTs, euro government bonds (EGBs), gilts, JGBs, and USD, EUR and GBP corporate credit, broken out by sector, rating and maturity.

Net supply is proxied by changes in Bloomberg index amount outstanding. This captures only index-eligible bonds and reflects debt approaching maturity one year ahead rather than current maturities, so it is an imperfect gauge. Index entries and exits such as fallen angels moving from IG to HY also change the figures.
